top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock. Magic-wavelength trapping is a separable invention that removes the lattice light shift so many atoms can be interrogated at once, it has been reproduced independently in Sr and Yb at several national laboratories, and the atomic structure behind the 1e-18 claims is well understood. I accept that it refines a measurement rather than opening a new field and that Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Lisdat and the PTB and NIST groups fall outside two names, but the citation can be limited to the invention and its realisation. That is a mature, correctly allocated prize and better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my field (electronic-structure theory, magnetism) and my Uppsala and Los Alamos ties have no link to Katori, Ye or their groups
